assets.purpose: Design reference only. User selected calmer water than this concept.
assets.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied actual Battleship Google TV screenshot into a believable native Android visual concept. Preserve the exact flat top-down square 10 by 10 enemy grid on the left, the existing right-hand navy command panel, all typography, coordinates, proportions, cyan square targeting cursor, and existing ship silhouettes. No tilted camera, no 3D perspective board, no UI redesign. Replace ONLY the flat water inside both boards with rich but restrained deep blue naval water: small-scale natural waves, slow-looking specular highlights and reflective wave ridges, no beach, no island, no underwater features. Water must remain dark enough for crisp grid lines, pale miss rings, coral hit crosses and cyan focus. The intended implementation is a lightweight Android shader and particles, so avoid large ocean surf or cinematic camera optics. Keep all text sharp and readable from a couch. Native TV app screenshot, edge-to-edge 16:9, no device frame. Preserve the app's existing dark blue, cyan, coral, and steel palette. This is a design reference, not a new bitmap UI asset. Show the peak of one missed missile at E5 in the main enemy board: a small translucent pale blue splash crown, a few distinct water droplets above it, and two widening rings that span about 1.5 cells. The effect has volume from shading but remains viewed directly overhead. The cyan cursor stays crisp on top. Only this one active impact. Keep own fleet board calm. Do not add a missile trail, camera shake, flames, or additional interface labels.
